title.narrative: OMR (Observatório do Meio Rural) - rural development research - core support
OMR (Observatório do Meio Rural) - rural development research - core support

description.narrative:
Denna beredning avser kärnstöd till OMR - Observatório do Meio Rural, en moçambikisk civilsamhällesorganisation vars uppdrag är "Produktion och spridning av kunskap genom forskning, för att påverka offentliga riktlinjer baserade på vetenskap, samt för att ge näring till lokala åtgärder och opinionsbildning, som syftar till hållbar och inkluderande landsbygdsutveckling."
OMR:s huvudmål är att "bidra till jordbruks- och landsbygdsutveckling i ett integrerat och tvärvetenskapligt perspektiv, genom forskning, studier och debatter om politik och andra jordbruksfrågor och landsbygdsutveckling. Bidra till att förbereda och följa upp politiken för jordbruks- och landsbygdsutveckling."
OMR:s huvudforskningsområden som beskrivs i dess strategiska plan för 2021-2025 är: (1) Offentlig politik och landsbygdsområden; (2) Affärsmässigt jordbruk, tidigare kända som landsbygdsutvecklingsmodeller; (2) Fattigdom, sociala ojämlikheter, kön och politiska konflikter; (3) Miljö (med fokus på klimatförändringar) kontra jordbruksproduktivitet (fokuserad på markens bördighet), avskogning och förändringar i produktionssystem för större motståndskraft mot klimatchocker och småskalig gruvdrift (garimpo) och, (4) Land och territorium.
När det gäller territoriellt fokus kommer OMR att fokusera på följande provinser: Cabo Delgado, Nampula (kust), Zambézia (Alta Zambézia) och mitten av landet (koncentrerat i Beira-korridoren).

This contribution is core support to the OMR - Observatório do Meio Rural, a Mozambican civil society organization whose mission is the "Production and dissemination of knowledge through research, in order to influence public policies based on scientific evidence, as well as to feed local action and advocacy, aiming at achieving sustainable and inclusive rural development."
OMR main objective is to "Contribute to agrarian and rural development in an integrated and interdisciplinary perspective, through research, studies and debates about policies and other agrarian issues and rural development. Contribute to the preparation and monitoring of agrarian and rural development policies."
OMR main research areas as in its Strategic Plan for 2021-2025 are: (1) Public policies and rural areas; (2) Agribusiness, formerly known as rural development models; (2) Poverty, social inequalities, gender, and political conflicts; (3) Environment (focused on climate change) versus agricultural productivity (focused on soil fertility), deforestation and changes in production systems for greater resilience to climate shocks and artisanal mining (garimpo) and, (4) Land and territory.
In terms of territorial focus, the OMR will focus on the following provinces: Cabo Delgado, Nampula (coastal), Zambézia (Alta Zambézia) and Centre of the country (concentrated in the Beira corridor).

title.narrative: Agreement to support Observatório do meio rural regarding core support
Decision to support Observatorio do meio Rural - core support

description.narrative:
OMR Key A Results 2025
In line with its strategic objective to contribute to agrarian and rural development through integrated and interdisciplinary research, policy analysis, and advocacy, the Observatório do Meio Rural (OMR) carried out a range of activities in 2025. These efforts were guided by the Strategic Plan 20212025 and annual activity plans, which define specific studies, publications, advocacy actions, and capacity-building initiatives.
Key results
The organisation implemented 22 of 23 planned multiannual research projects across five thematic lines and produced 63 publications, addressing nationally relevant issues such as economic development models, land and natural resource governance, climate change, biodiversity, extractive industries, post conflict dynamics and youth integration throughout Mozambique. OMR attained high public visibility, with its research cited 241 times in national and international media, 195,830 website visits, growing social media reach, and the successful organization of the 2025 Annual Conference, which brought together 503 participants and was opened by the country Head of Cooperation, reinforcing OMRs role as a key platform for national policy dialogue. Through evidence based but selective advocacy, OMR contributed to key policy processes, including land and environmental legislation, carbon market regulation, civic space and public finance management. Institutionally, OMR strengthened its governance and sustainability through the approval of new long-term strategies, completion of a midterm strategic evaluation, advances in human resources management, digital transformation and continuous staff capacity development
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
